name: EU accessibility evidence monitor for small sites
demand: The addressable population is unverified: I found no official count of EAA-covered websites and no product-specific user or install count. Useful proxies, with different denominators: Eurostat reports 34 million EU enterprises in 2024; in 2025, 20.3% of enterprises with at least 10 employees reported e-commerce sales of at least 1% of turnover, and 79.02% of EU enterprises reported having a website. Neither figure isolates eligible consumer-facing services. A Belgian marketing agency reports average monthly Google Ads search estimates from 28 Sep 2026 of 260 for “European Accessibility Act” in Belgium and 480 in the Netherlands; for “WCAG,” 590 and 3,600 respectively. Treat those keyword figures as third-party, unverified estimates. A WordPress accessibility checker reports 10,000+ active installations, but it is not this product and does not prove paid demand. The EAA applies to specified products and services, including e-commerce, from 28 June 2025; service micro-enterprises under the stated thresholds are exempt, so “small sites” is too broad a target. Sources: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/SEPDF/cache/1168.pdf?v=8330321832337163 ; https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/15216629/23732306/KS-01-26-010-EN-N.pdf/d1f4be4f-4b8a-f150-2d4d-13918a3e16ee ; https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/SEPDF/cache/22286.pdf?v=8346100741086513 ; https://www.customerimpact.be/en/blog/european-accessibility-act-lead-generation/ ; https://wordpress.org/plugins/accessibility-checker/ ; https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/accessibility-goods-services/
prices: Current public asking prices show a crowded ladder: EAA Compliance lists €149, €449 and €990/month and includes an evidence ledger and coverage matrix; A11yProof lists €29/month for monitoring and €99/month for its EAA tier; EAA Watch lists €9/month; Inkluso lists €49/month or €490/year; EU Conformance Hub lists €300–€800/month for monitoring. These are advertised prices, not verified transactions or revenue. Sources: https://eaacompliance.org/pricing ; https://a11yproof.talivio.com/pricing ; https://eaa.steadyrobots.com/ ; https://inkluso.eu/en/ ; https://www.conformancehub.eu/pricing

revenue_proof.claim: UNVERIFIED: no receipts, transaction data, paid-customer count, MRR, or churn evidence found. EAA Compliance’s page advertises paid plans, which is pricing evidence only, not proof that customers paid.
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: Unverified; page observed 2026-10-23, but no underlying payment date is disclosed.

copy_speed: Fast and already demonstrated. Rampsight dates its first public release, including weekly monitoring and reports, to 2 Sep 2026. OverlayQA says scheduled accessibility monitoring has been live since Jul 2026. EAA Compliance’s changelog dates its project to 14 Apr and crawler prototype to 22 Apr 2026, both labeled pre-release; its current product page advertises the same evidence-ledger and criteria-mapping wedge. Accessiway announced continuous monitoring and issue management on 20 Apr 2026, just before the 23 Apr comparison cutoff. Sources: https://rampsight.com/changelog ; https://overlayqa.com/accessibility-monitoring/ ; https://eaacompliance.org/changelog ; https://www.accessiway.com/blog/platform-launch-pr
platform_risk: Moderate. A public-page scanner can operate without a platform owner, but CMS/app-store distribution would add platform-policy and integration dependencies. I found no independently verified official partner providing the full mapping-plus-evidence workflow. The larger risk is substitution: established free tools and shared testing engines make scans easy to copy. W3C says automated tools cannot check every accessibility aspect and human judgement is required. Source: https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/tools/selecting/ ; https://wordpress.org/plugins/accessibility-checker/
defensible_asset: Potential rules and history asset, but the proposed moat is already directly contested: EAA Compliance advertises a legal coverage matrix, guided manual audits and an append-only evidence ledger, with its changelog dating that ledger to 19 May 2026. Legal texts and WCAG are public, so a mapping table alone is replicable; per-site histories may create modest switching costs if customers rely on them. I found no evidence of a network effect. A stronger asset would require demonstrably maintained jurisdiction-specific decision rules and validated, longitudinal remediation evidence. Sources: https://eaacompliance.org/pricing ; https://eaacompliance.org/changelog ; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.L_.2019.151.01.0070.01.ENG
build_effort: Estimate: moderate for a self-serve public-page scanner and scan-history MVP; high for a trustworthy evidence product with jurisdiction rules, manual-review states, authenticated journeys, audit exports, security, privacy and integrations. Calendar time and cost are unverified. Ongoing standards interpretation cannot safely be fully automated: W3C requires human judgement, and EU member states implement the directive nationally. Sources: https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/tools/selecting/ ; https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/accessibility-goods-services/ ; https://eaacompliance.org/pricing
channel: Use search-led guidance and a free eligibility check/scanner, then WordPress or Shopify listings and integrations, plus permission-based agency or accessibility-specialist partnerships. No cold email, SMS, DMs or calls. Contextual search ads are a possible test channel; for UK users, the ICO says storage/access technologies for online advertising require consent and contextual ads are easier to align with privacy obligations. Check local advertising and privacy requirements in each destination country. Sources: https://www.customerimpact.be/en/blog/european-accessibility-act-lead-generation/ ; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/how-do-the-rules-apply-to-online-advertising/ ; https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/accessibility-goods-services/
owner_hours_per_week: Target estimate: 3–5 hours/week after launch, including support, admin and channel oversight, conditional on self-serve onboarding and agent-run operations. This is unverified; legal-rule review, false positives and customer edge cases could push it over the limit.
automation_reason: Estimate for all recurring work: agents can run scheduled scans, compare results, assemble evidence reports, handle billing and routine support, and draft/search-optimize content. Human review remains necessary for legal scope and rule changes, subjective accessibility checks, exceptions, quality control and partnership decisions. W3C explicitly says tools cannot automate all checks. Sources: https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/tools/selecting/ ; https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/accessibility-goods-services/
moat_assessment: The stated moat is plausible in principle but weak as a differentiator today. EAA Compliance already advertises essentially the proposed evidence-ledger and legal-mapping combination; cheaper monitoring alternatives exist, and the underlying rules and standards are public. Site histories provide only soft switching costs unless users need durable, trusted audit provenance and cannot easily export or recreate it. Sources: https://eaacompliance.org/pricing ; https://a11yproof.talivio.com/pricing ; https://eaa.steadyrobots.com/ ; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.L_.2019.151.01.0070.01.ENG
desk_test: Within one day, make a no-code page for one narrow eligible segment, show a sample dated evidence report and a clearly labeled planned €29/month offer, and add a voluntary waitlist button. Share only where self-promotion is permitted in relevant public communities or through an opt-in partner; no cold contact. The €29 anchor matches an existing advertised monitoring tier, so sign-ups would test interest in the evidence workflow, not prove unique willingness to pay. Source for comparator price: https://a11yproof.talivio.com/pricing
red_flags: The original cheap-survivor case is materially weakened by direct overlap and documented 2026 entrants. “Small web publishers” is a poor legal targeting rule: the EAA covers specified services, not every website, and service micro-enterprises below the stated thresholds are exempt. The 28 June 2025 application date is already past, not a future commencement trigger. Automated scans cannot establish full accessibility or legal compliance. No verified revenue or churn evidence was found; public plan prices do not prove demand. Sources: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/accessibility-goods-services/ ; https://rampsight.com/changelog ; https://overlayqa.com/accessibility-monitoring/ ; https://eaacompliance.org/changelog ; https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/tools/selecting/ ; https://eaacompliance.org/pricing
